attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The 'arguably' hedge applies only to there being some generalization. The 'wrong generalization' clause is firm and limited to the monkey-chess example. This is an interpretive observation about one video.

contract.note: Testing only the observable core (a realistic-looking board that breaks chess rules) is a fair, ordinary reading. The interpretive 'wrong generalization' part can't be checked and is rightly set aside.

evidence.note: NextBigFuture (Feb 25, 2024) repeats Marcus's description of the 7x7 board and three kings. It relays the speaker and is not an independent look at the video.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs an independent description of the video's board. The only item just restates Marcus's own account, and the speaker's statements can't prove themselves. No independent source confirms or rules out the invalid board, so the claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: A third-person closing line Marcus wrote in his own post. He wrote and endorses it.

semantics.note: The rhetorical 'astonished' frame is dropped and the substantive retrospective claim is kept, including its 'even with ever-greater data' qualifier. That is faithful.

contract.note: Reading 'struggled mightily' as substantial, repeated difficulties that can coexist with improvement is an ordinary reading, not stretched for or against him. Limiting evidence to before February 17, 2024 fits the retrospective claim.

evidence.note: VISOR (Oct 2023): text-to-image models get spatial relations right in under 40% of cases despite photorealism. Supports the world-consistency difficulty.
Faith and Fate (2023): LLM performance on multistep compositional tasks falls off sharply as complexity rises. Supports the reasoning difficulty.
Meta's own disclosure: 40% more pretraining tokens, modest TruthfulQA truthfulness, and gains with scale and fine-tuning. Shows the data growth and partial progress.
OpenAI concedes GPT-4 still hallucinates and makes reasoning errors, while reporting gains. This is a company disclosure, but it admits a limitation of its own product.

reviews.rationale: Pre-February 2024 evaluations show repeated failures in spatial and world consistency (e1) and in multistep reasoning (e2). Factuality problems are acknowledged in model reports (e3, e4) alongside larger training data. The improvements reported in e3 and e4 are allowed by the contract and don't meet its condition that the difficulties had been substantially overcome.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A firm claim about how Sora works and its lack of global representations. The paraphrase matches both the pixel-reconstruction sentence and the forest/trees metaphor.

contract.note: Treating 'pixels' loosely and reading the metaphors as a lack of whole-object or scene representations fits his surrounding text ('no internal model', 'no global comprehension'). The reading is fair, but whether the claim holds depends on it.

evidence.note: A Feb 27, 2024 review describes Sora as a diffusion transformer over latent spacetime patches. It reconstructs the architecture from public information and does not examine internal representations.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs architecture documentation or direct studies showing whether whole-object representations exist. The packet holds only a secondary architectural summary, which neither shows a local-only mechanism nor shows global representations. The packet itself notes no representation study was found.
